title: Doc S Possible NDE 6777
content: We humans often have a propensity to over describe our experiences. We all get programmed to respond to various experiences. I wish to be brief and to the point. I was poisoned inadvertently at a Mexican Restaurant. I ate food that someone had poured toxic levels of Mono Sodium Glutamate, (MSG) into. I arrived home several hours later under extreme physical duress. I went to the bathroom and tried to throw up, but the pain in the top of my head was overwhelming my senses. Suddenly, in my mind's eye, there was a very small yellow twinkle that seemed as though it was moving towards me until it encompassed my entire being as it seemed. There was the seeming appearance of a glittering, draped, flowing black dynamic tunnel of sorts. It led to a yellow bright light. As it approached, and the light fell at my feet, I felt the pain in my head relieved. I saw no one and heard nothing. I felt a very satisfying feeling of well being. As soon as this happened, I sensed in my mind, as if I was asking myself for some reason, ‘Well Doc, it is up to you.’ I felt that the meaning was whether to enter the light or not. I reflected very briefly, and ‘said’, ‘not now. I have a very ill cancer-ridden wife who needs my help to survive and depends on my daily nursing.’ I was then instantly thrust away from the light and the tunnel disappeared. I found myself in the bathroom. I felt terrific pain, which continued off and on for the next twenty four exhausting hours. I had the same experience happen two more times that night. The last time, I requested that it not occur again. That was my experience. I had never studied the near death experience before, and really had no concept of it prior to this event. Since then, I have done some research. I do not call it a religious or spiritual event. It seems it may have been some instinct that triggers whenever we are at a final moment of life. Some say that it rallies from the inner mind, perhaps the Pineal Gland. My interest now is to clarify the nature of the experience, and just what triggers such a response. ---- NDERF response: A near death experience is medically inexplicable. Nobody knows what causes it. This experience is hard to classify because there is no evidence as to whether this was medically an imminently life-threatening event. It is a possible near death experience unless there is more information on this point.
